newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast lt. crudes fall, despite ANS deal.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast lt. crudes fall, despite ANS deal.

text.p: Outright prices for U.S West Coast light crudes fell with West Texas Intermediate (WTI), offsetting tighter differentials Friday, a day after BP sold to a major California refiner, traders said.
Traders said BP sold a full cargo of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude at minus 0.90 cents late Thursday. The sale raised the discount on ANS 10 cents over the previous sale.
A trader said expectations of fewer Canadian imports forced the refinery to pay higher prices for ANS.
"The guys up in Canada seem to think they're going to be thin," a trader said.
Northwest refiners typically buy Canadian light crudes as an alternative to ANS.
Despite the lower discount, ANS outright prices fell to $19.65/19.85 a barrel, off 15 cents from Thursday.
One trader said they bought a 400,000-barrel cargo of Colombia South Blend crude earlier this week. The blend, an ANS lookalike, is slated for early April delivery, the trader said.
Line 63 prices stood unchanged at postings plus $0.95 - $1.05.

Kern River heavy crude prices rose, with discounts tightening. A deal was heard done earlier this week at 0.45 cents a barrel under postings, a sharp increase over previous discounts. Outright prices were talked $14.14/14.50 a barrel, versus 13.84/14.04 a barrel earlier this week.
